rounds.q: On average, how many years does a pet dog live?
rounds.why: US vet records from 2013 to 2019 put it at 12.7 years, and a study of 584,734 UK dogs found 12.5.
rounds.src: Montoya et al., Frontiers in Veterinary Science 2023 (Banfield US clinic data); Dogs Trust and Liverpool John Moores University, Scientific Reports 2024 (UK dogs)
rounds.fun: About 13 years of walks, belly rubs and treats. Every one of them counts!

rounds.q: How many puppies are in a dog's average litter?
rounds.why: The exact average is 5.4, from 3.5 pups for the tiniest breeds to 7.1 for giant breeds.
rounds.src: Borge et al., Theriogenology, study of 10,810 litters in 224 breeds (2006-2007 data)
rounds.fun: About 5 puppies per litter, and giant breeds can bring 7. That's a lot of tiny paws!

rounds.q: What % of US households own a dog?
rounds.why: That's about 71 million homes, per the pet industry. A vets' group survey found 45.5%, so counts vary.
rounds.src: American Pet Products Association, State of the Industry (2025 data); AVMA Pet Ownership and Demographics Sourcebook (2024 data)
rounds.fun: Around half of US homes have a dog. Odds are good there's a wagging tail on your street!

rounds.q: How many teeth does an adult dog have?
rounds.why: Puppies start with 28 baby teeth, and adult cats have just 30.
rounds.src: Merck Veterinary Manual, Dental Development of Dogs and of Cats
rounds.fun: 42 teeth! A grown dog has 14 more than it did as a puppy. Big smile, big chews!

rounds.q: How many billions of dollars did Americans spend on pets in 2025?
rounds.why: That's up 3.7% from 2024, and it's expected to reach $165 billion in 2026.
rounds.src: American Pet Products Association, State of the Industry (2025 data)
rounds.fun: $158 billion on our furry friends. They sure are worth every treat!
